transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-08
Start: 14:00 PST
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Nina Gomez (Redwood), Tom Reyes (Aurora), Priya Singh, Liam Ortega, Sara Holt, Ben Cho

Summary (auto): Weekly POC check-in to review model selection results, discuss pinning and fallback strategy after last week's benchmark.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for jumping on, can you hear me okay?
[00:07] Tom: Yep, loud and clear, thanks Maya.
[00:15] Maya: Alright quick agenda - review the perf numbers Arjun sent, discuss which models to pin for the pilot, talk rollback/fallback triggers, and next steps. If we run over we'll pick up in the security deep dive next week.
[00:30] Arjun: I can run through the numbers, just a quick note, we've got the spreadsheet up at https://redwood.app/shared/poc/aurora/pinned-models-v2.xlsx - it's got latency P50/P95, token cost, and quality evals by prompt set.
[00:45] Priya: I opened it, thanks. One thing I noticed the P95 for the quantized 13B variant was spiking at peak - is that expected with batching?
[01:02] Arjun: Yeah so for the 13B-quant we saw some tail latency at bursty QPS because of compaction overhead and KV cache misses; that's on pages 4-5, the distribution chart. We can tune batch windows and enable prefix caching to lower that.
[01:20] Liam: Remind me, which model variants are we seriously considering pinning?
[01:25] Maya: Right now top contenders: redwood-13b-quant-v2 (cost efficient), redwood-13b-fp16-v1 (lower latency but higher cost), and redwood-70b-int8 (higher quality on complex prompts but heavier). We also tested open-compat models like claude-2-lite in the evals for comparison.
[01:50] Tom: The quality gap at long-form finance reasoning is notable for the 70b variant, but the token cost is, uh, very different. We have to balance latency for user-facing chat vs nightly batch summarization where cost matters less.
[02:10] Arjun: Agreed. One idea is route chat to pin redwood-13b-fp16, and route long-form tasks to the 70b with a different SLA - that's a routing policy config we can set in the console.
[02:30] Sara: From security, we need to ensure any model pinned in Dedicated or Private mode meets our data residency and KMS policies; we can't have customer data leave the VPC. Can you confirm where pinning actually lives?
[02:42] Maya: Good call. Pinning metadata is in the control plane but we can deploy on Aurora's VPC for Private mode; the control plane can be customer-managed, and keys can be in your KMS/HSM. We'll send the architecture note.
[02:58] Ben: Also audit logs - can we get per-request attribution tied to our SSO IDs?
[03:05] Arjun: Yes, we support token-level tracing and integrate with your SIEM - audit logs provide per-request tokens, route, model version, and can be forwarded to your S3 or Splunk. There's a small note in the security FAQs.
[03:25] Maya: Back to pinning mechanics - Arjun, walk through the rollback/fallback proposal you suggested last week.
[03:33] Arjun: Sure. Two layers: first, a hard pin which ties a route to a model version; second, a fallback policy that defines compatible variants to use if the pinned model is unavailable or exceeds an error/latency threshold. For example pin redwood-13b-quant-v2, fallback to redwood-13b-fp16-v1 if timeout rate > 2% or P95 > 1200ms for two consecutive minutes.
[04:00] Priya: How do you define compatibility? Some models have different tokenization or output differences and that may break our downstream parsers.
[04:10] Arjun: We define compatibility by architecture family and tokenizer. We flagged compatible pairs in the catalog; we'll include a compatibility matrix in the doc. For more structured outputs we recommend function-calling stability tests before pinning.
[04:30] Tom: Any automated canary rollout or A/B support so we can shift 5-10% traffic and compare quality?
[04:38] Maya: Yes, console supports canary rollouts and traffic splits; you can measure regressions with our eval hooks. That's part of Redwood Optimize integration.
[04:50] Liam: In last week's eval the 13b-quant had similar accuracy on our prompt set but hallucinated more on the legal-citation style prompts, which is concerning.
[05:03] Arjun: For hallucinations we saw that too; the value there was tuning temperature and forcing a higher recency window for few-shot context. Also sometimes quantized weights can slightly alter rare token probabilities. We can try a 2-token padding strategy and re-evaluate.
[05:25] Maya: Okay so do we have consensus? Tom, what would you be comfortable pinning for the pilot traffic (50k monthly tokens expected)?
[05:34] Tom: My vote: pin redwood-13b-quant-v2 for general chat, but keep a route pinned to 70b-int8 for high-value summarization tasks. Also need an immediate fallback to fp16 in case of degradation.
[05:48] Sara: From security, if we go Dedicated we'll need the dedicated pool within our VPC and keys under our KMS. We need the dedicated confirmation in writing for procurement.
[06:00] Maya: We'll include that in the follow-up email - architecture + KMS flows.
[06:07] Priya: Quick question on metrics - can we export per-model P95 to BigQuery for our dashboards?
[06:12] Arjun: Yep, metrics sink supports BigQuery and Prometheus; we can set up a metric stream.
[06:20] [brief pause]
[06:30] Nina: I've got a note about automatic rollback windows - for the POC we recommend conservative thresholds: P95 > 1.2s for 3 consecutive minutes or error rate > 1.5% to trigger fallback. These are tunable.
[06:45] Tom: Sounds reasonable. How does the rollback affect in-flight sessions? Do you drain or abruptly switch?
[06:53] Arjun: We do connection-aware switch: inflight requests finish on the old model but new requests are routed to fallback. For chat sessions we persist the session state so user sees continuity. There may be slight change in output style, so we recommend a small notice or a re-eval if it's critical.
[07:12] Liam: About rollbacks - we had an incident in-house where a model change caused our parser to break because of a trailing newline difference. Any guardrails here?
[07:21] Arjun: We have a pre-deploy validation step - you can upload a set of canonical prompts and expected structured outputs for smoke tests. If the fallback model fails more than X% of smoke tests, the system will not auto-fallback and will instead alert and hold. We'll include smoke test config examples.
[07:45] Sara: Also need SAML/SSO alignment and RBAC so only certain roles can change pinning. Can you surface audit trails for who changed a pin?
[07:55] Maya: Yes, audit + RBAC is standard; we can map to your IdP groups.
[08:05] Tom: One ask - can we get a short runbook for emergency rollback steps, like manual pin override via API?
[08:12] Arjun: Absolutely, we'll include the curl samples and console screenshots.
[08:18] Maya: Let's talk timeline - by next Monday (12/13) we want two models chosen. Benchmarks run by Redwood and Aurora to validate.
[08:28] Tom: Agreed. We'll finalize models and run a production-sampled 10k prompt set.
[08:33] Priya: About cost numbers - I see token cost estimates but not account-level monthly spend projection for our expected volume. Can you produce that?
[08:42] Maya: Yes I'll add a projected monthly cost sheet for 50k tokens/month and a high-usage scenario.
[08:50] [09:00] Arjun: Small note on quantization: the int8 builds are stable but when we switch kernels for different hardware there are corner cases on Nvidia vs AMD. If you go Dedicated we'll verify target hardware and test kernel alignment.
[09:18] Ben: Are there any limitations for private on-prem deployment?
[09:22] Arjun: On-prem is supported but requires the customer's infra team to run the runtime; we'd ship the package and the control plane can be air-gapped. Performance tuning is included but it's a slightly longer onboarding (3-6 weeks).
[09:38] Liam: Ok good. Anything else on technical?
[09:42] Tom: Can we run a 24h fallback stress test to simulate node failures in the dedicated pool? Want to see real fallback switching.
[09:50] Maya: Yes we can schedule that - Arjun to coordinate a test window.
[09:55] Arjun: I'll propose windows for the week of 12/14. We'll simulate node loss and also throttle a model to trigger the latency threshold.
[10:05] Maya: Security Q: Sara, you'll join the deeper security session on 12/15?
[10:10] Sara: Yes, tentatively 12/15 10am PT works for us.
[10:14] [10:30] Arjun: Quick clarifying point on catalog comparisons - the catalog page includes recommended pin pairs and compatibility notes, sometimes the model name in the UI is a little different from the binary (e.g., redwood-13b-quant-v2 might appear as rwd-13q-v2 in some logs) - just a heads up for mapping.
[10:45] Priya: Noted, that mapping caused confusion in last week's logs.
[11:00] Tom: Any blockers from Redwood side?
[11:04] Maya: No blockers - just deliverables: perf spreadsheet, pinning config snippet, rollback runbook, and canary setup examples.
[11:12] Liam: On testing structured outputs we'll share our parser tests by Friday.
[11:18] Sara: We'll share security compliance matrix by Thursday.
[11:22] Maya: Great. Let's recap actions.
[11:30] [Recap]
Maya: Action items - Maya to share perf spreadsheet and monthly cost projection; Arjun to send pinning config + rollback runbook + propose fallback test windows; Tom to select two models and produce the 10k prompt set; Sara to share security matrix. We'll target the 12/14 fallback test and 12/15 security review.

[11:55] Tom: Thanks everyone, this was helpful.
[12:00] Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up with an email and links. Bye.

Notes: transcript includes occasional mislabels and short pauses; audio-based auto-transcripts sometimes concatenated tokens (e.g., "rwd-13q-v2" vs "redwood-13b-quant-v2").
